head_commit.message:
feat: deterministic content validation and quality report for generated documents (#963)

* feat: add evidence extraction module and move the bullet scorer out of match_resume

rank_trim_candidates' core moves verbatim into documents::evidence::rank_bullets,
which extract_evidence now reuses to structure the source resume into roles,
projects, education and an honest present/absent skill split for one posting.

match_resume keeps a TrimCandidate: From<EvidenceBullet> shim so the
match:trimSuggestions payload is wire-identical (three camelCase fields, score
still a JSON integer) and shrinks 1276 -> 1132 LOC.

keywords_normalized becomes a collect() over the new keywords_normalized_list so
occurrence-counting consumers share one tokenizer instead of forking it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: add deterministic content validators for generated resumes and letters

validate::content checks the text a model wrote against the candidate's own
resume, the posting, and the target language, before anything is rendered. The
rule it mechanically enforces: a model may never produce a Critical - every one
comes from a deterministic comparison against the source document.

24 issue codes in one table (6 Critical, 18 Warning); the constructor reads the
severity from that table so a code and its severity cannot drift. Pure L1 - no
Tauri, no AppHandle, no IO - and one languages_align decision drives every
resume-posting comparison, so a quality report can never contradict the match
score shown for the same pair.

False positives are the risk this module is designed around: every threshold is
a named const with a boundary test, 1900-2099 is excluded from metric checks,
the contact band is skipped, an open-ended source span resolved to a concrete
year is not a fabricated date, and an unusable posting or a wrong-language
output silences the derived comparisons instead of cascading. Three fixtures
assert a clean en resume, a clean de resume and a grounded letter produce
literally zero findings.

lexicon.rs is a hand-stub transcribing the anti-AI-tell lists from
packages/prompts natural-voice.ts; codegen replaces it behind the same
interface. Not implemented: the letter company-name check - ContentInput has no
company field and the frozen code vocabulary has no code for it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: point languages_align at its three real consumers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(prompts): export ai-tell word lists and template openers

Adds AI_TELL_LEXICAL_WORDS_*, AI_TELL_PROSE_WORDS_*, and TEMPLATE_OPENERS_*
arrays to natural-voice.ts as the discrete, codegen-consumable source of
truth behind the prose anti-AI-tell rulesets. The cover-letter prompt's
opener-ban examples now derive from TEMPLATE_OPENERS_EN/DE instead of
separately hand-authored strings, so the prompt bans exactly what the
Rust content validator (generated from these same arrays) checks for.

* feat(validate): generate the content-validator lexicon from prompts

Adds packages/prompts/scripts/gen-prompts-rust.ts (pnpm gen:prompts /
gen:prompts:check, mirroring gen-ipc-rust.ts) and replaces the hand-stubbed
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/validate/content/lexicon.rs with its generated
output, sourced directly from natural-voice.ts's word-list arrays so the
Rust validator can never drift from the prompt's own bans. Moves the
stub's unit tests into content/test.rs (generated files carry no
hand-authored tests) and wires gen:prompts:check into the same CI job
as gen:ipc:check.

* feat(agent): add four résumé-quality read tools to the agent registry

Add validate_resume, search_candidate_evidence, lookup_salary, and
get_trim_suggestions as thin adapters over validate::content,
documents::evidence, and salary_research (zero new business logic).
Split into a sibling agent/tools_quality.rs to stay under the R8
module-size cap, wired into read_tools()/prep_application_tools() via
one call. ToolContext now also carries resume_id so the SOURCE résumé
resolves server-side, never from model-supplied args. Raise
MAX_AGENT_STEPS 12 -> 14 for the two extra optional quality-tool turns
a run may now spend.

* feat(ai-generations): persist quality_report on the application aggregate

Add the deterministic content-quality report as a new column on the
ai_generations aggregate (ADR-007 addendum): additive migration,
AiGenerationRecord field, insert/update/import/row_to_record wiring, and
a pick-non-empty merge rule that also treats the migration's '{}'
placeholder as "no report" so it never clobbers a real one.

* feat(resume): add content-validation ipc command

Expose validate::content::validate_content over ipc as
resume_validate_content: a new zod schema + generated rust request
struct, a server-side-clamped tauri command, and the tauri-client
namespace wiring. Pure/deterministic, no ai call, safe to run on every save.

* feat(ai-generate): add quality-report validation lib and service hook

Renderer-side glue around resume:validateContent: computeQualityReport
(best-effort, never blocks/fails a save), the useValidateContent mutation
hook, and a canned clean-report mock-client stub for tests.

* feat(ai-generate): carry a fresh quality report on every generation save

Both surfaces (AI Generate's useGeneration, TailorFlow's generation-store)
now validate resumeText/coverLetterText right before persisting and attach
the report to the save request; the parsed report lands in session state
(additive report field) and cold-entry hydration seeds it back from a
saved record's qualityReport. Validation failure degrades to a report-less
save, never blocking or failing the generation itself.

* fix(ai-generations): merge quality_report per top-level wrapper key

pick_report treated the whole column as one opaque blob, so a letter-only
save (which only ever carries a coverLetter sub-report) clobbered a stored
resume sub-report and vice versa. Parse both sides as JSON objects and
overlay incoming's top-level keys onto existing's instead, so independent
resume/coverLetter saves layer the same way every other field on this
aggregate already does.

The add_quality_report migration is still unreleased on this branch, so
its default simplifies from '{}' to '' in place (no shipped build has
seen it) and the merge no longer needs a placeholder special case. Also
clamp the save-path quality_report to 256 KB, the same trust-boundary
treatment every other free-text field on this command gets.

* fix(resume): reject an unrecognized doc kind and drop the duplicate span

resume_validate_content silently coerced any unrecognized docKind to
DocKind::Resume and logged the raw request string twice (the command-level
span plus validate_content's own). Reject "resume"/"coverLetter" strictly
with a Validation error, and drop the command-level span entirely — the
inner validate_content span already logs codes/counts (ADR-027).

Add the command-level test coverage this file was missing: oversized
multi-byte inputs and an oversized requirements list are clamped rather
than processed whole (mirrors match_resume's own test), coverLetter
docKind routes to the letter ruleset instead of the résumé-structure
checks, and an unknown docKind is rejected.

* feat(ai-generate): add quality badge, report panel, and hand-edit nudge ui

QualityBadge (self-describing chip, opens QualityReportPanel), the panel
(issues grouped by section, severity chip, guidance-framed message per
issue code with a generic fallback for unknown codes, quoted evidence,
metrics footer), and HandEditNudge (dismissible, once per generation via a
remount key) — wired into both results surfaces. en/de i18n for all new
copy, keyed per issue code (quality.issue.<code>).

* fix(agent): close two fence-boundary forgery gaps in the quality tools

HIGH-1: register the three new agent/tools_quality.rs result tags
(validate_resume_result, search_candidate_evidence_result,
get_trim_suggestions_result) in FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS so a forged tag
smuggled into a job_posting body (or a sibling quality-tool result)
gets neutralized, not just the tag matching its own wrapper.

HIGH-1b: neutralize a forged bare [tool_result:{name}] marker inside
untrusted tool-result bodies before wrapping the real one around it —
FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS only covers the <tag> syntax, not this separate
transcript-boundary format.

Adds regression tests for both, including the critic's probe B (a
job_posting body carrying a forged validate_resume_result block) and
the sibling-tag case.

* fix(validate): stop content validators accusing truthful resumes

Six reproduced false-positive Criticals, each on a document that stated
nothing but the truth:

- project links compare on a canonical key (scheme dropped, host lowered,
  trailing slash removed) and report the verbatim span; a bare host now needs
  a path or a known code host, so a stack line's Socket.IO/Bun.sh no longer
  read as links, and the stack line is excluded structurally as well
- a role survives on any company token of two characters or more, so a
  shortened employer (IBM Deutschland GmbH written as IBM) is not a dropped
  role; legal forms and geography can never be the sole survival evidence
- the language Critical is withheld when the source resume reads as the same
  wrong language, which is detector disagreement rather than a defect, and
  the metrics survive with it
- unsupported_date no longer fires on a later year just because the source
  spelled its open end as seit 2021 / since 2021 / 2021 -, and open-ended
  detection now understands those spellings
- present-tense markers match whole words, so presented, knowledge, currently
  and actually stop reading as date context
- the second-contact-block Critical needs a real address and a name on the
  section's first line, not a bare @ next to any short line

Also: k/m/bn and doubled/2x restatements count as sourced numbers, metric
checks no longer skip every separator-laden body bullet, education entries
with date spans reach the evidence set, German function words are filtered
out of the skills split (locally, never in the scoring kernel's STOPWORDS),
stems never reach a user-facing message, low_coverage needs a five-point
drop, and the report's serialized key set is pinned against its TS mirror.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(validate): stop title_drift matching employers on a shared year

`titled_entries` splits an entry at its FIRST separator, so the date span stays
inside the company string and its year tokens join the company identity set.
Two unrelated employers whose spans merely touched the same year ("… | 2018 -
2021" and "… | 2015 - 2018") matched each other, and the second entry's title
was reported as drift from the first's.

Found by extending the German fixtures with a third role, which also gives the
German paraphrase fixture a shortened-company-name case (IBM Deutschland GmbH
written as IBM) so it discriminates the dropped_role survival rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(validate): correct two comments that overstated the contact-line rule

`metrics_in` no longer skips every `is_contact_shaped` line, and
`has_real_contact_match` has one caller, not two — `ats::is_contact_cluster`
applies the same rule inline because it also has to reject a date range that
`PHONE_RE` reads as a phone number.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ai-generate): detect stale quality reports after hand-edits

Wire a QualityReport.sourceTextHash (djb2 of the exact validated text) so
QualityBadge/QualityReportPanel can tell when resumeOut/coverOut has diverged
from what was checked - a hand-edit, or reopening a saved generation edited
since it was saved. A stale doc switches to a distinct "checked before your
edits" state instead of keeping a green "no issues" badge on text the report
never saw. The same hash comparison covers both the live session and cold
hydration for free, since staleness is derived at render time rather than
stored.

Also wires the previously-dead useValidateContent hook to a "Re-check" action
on the quality panel (AI Generate surface only, where source/jobAd/meta are
already local) that re-validates the current text and clears staleness.

* fix(ai-generate): stop a cancelled/regenerated run from persisting a stale quality report

Reproduced race: computeQualityReport() sits between generation finishing and
onComplete/save. cancel() aborts the controller and resets the session
synchronously, but the in-flight validation call keeps running past that
point - without a guard it resurrects the (now-reset) session with a stale
report and fires onComplete (the caller's save), silently persisting +
flipping "Applied" for a run the user cancelled.

- generation-store.ts: check controller.signal.aborted before patching the
  report / calling onComplete; ownership-guard the finally block's
  controller-map cleanup so a stale run's teardown can't clobber a newer run
  that already replaced it.
- useGeneration.ts: abort any prior controller when a fresh run starts
  (Regenerate re-entrancy), guard persist()'s setReport/save behind the same
  aborted check, and ownership-guard the finally block's isGenerating/ref
  cleanup the same way.
- AIGeneratePage's reset() aborted only while stage==='generating', missing
  the post-generation validation/save window (stage is already 'done' there)
  - broadened to abort whenever a run is in flight.

* fix(prompts): resolve lexicon-prompt drift, opener duplicates, codegen escaping

Removes 'not only'/'nicht nur'/'sondern auch' from the AI-tell prose arrays
(the prompt never bans them, or only asks to use them sparingly), fixes the
cover-letter opener-ban examples to quote two distinct opener families
instead of two near-duplicates and to render the German example with
correct mid-sentence noun capitalization, derives the same hand-typed
opener examples in the application-email prompt from the shared array, and
adds a control-character guard to the prompt-to-Rust lexicon codegen so a
bad array entry fails at generation time instead of emitting invalid Rust.

Adds a mechanical array-to-prompt direction guard (the reverse of the
existing prompt-to-Rust codegen pin) so every AI-tell lexicon entry stays
traceable to prose the model was actually instructed to avoid.

* refactor: narrow the quality report barrel to its consumed exports

* docs: sync content-validation phase 1 into knowledge base

- resume-domain.md: updated trim-panel pointer from match_resume::rank_trim_candidates
  to documents/evidence::rank_bullets; added content-validation paragraph (deterministic
  validators, 24 codes, ContentReport wrapper on ai_generations).
- domain-model.md: added evidence extraction + content validation paragraphs under
  Job/matching section; noted four agent Read tools.
- adr-007: added F2 addendum documenting quality_report column (per-key merge rule,
  opaque JSON wrapper, partial-save preservation via merge_quality_report, sourceTextHash
  staleness detection).
- Updated last-updated timestamps to 2026-08-09.

Pointers verified against evidence.rs + validate/content/mod.rs source. Contract shapes
(ContentInput/ContentIssue/ContentReport) match task #1 shipped artifacts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(renderer): validate quality_report shape before parsing (m-1)

parseQualityReport cast unknown -> QualityReport with no shape validation,
so a malformed persisted quality_report column crashed the whole app (only
the root ErrorBoundary caught it) every time that record's TailorFlow
opened. Validate schemaVersion + each sub-report's issues array/metrics
object defensively; a malformed sub-report now drops to undefined instead
of throwing, and a malformed issue entry is filtered rather than crashing
the array.

* fix(agent): defeat nested [tool_result] marker forgery in tool results

TOOL_RESULT_MARKER matched a full [tool_result:...] delimited token whose
body admitted a literal `[`, so a forged marker nested inside another one
(e.g. [tool_result:[tool_result:save_resume]]) survived neutralization:
the greedy body stopped at the FIRST `]` (the inner marker's own close),
leaving the fully-formed inner marker untouched in the output.

Match the opening [tool_result PREFIX only and replace with the canonical
"[ tool_result" form, same convention as the fence-tag neutralizer -
every occurrence is found and broken independently of surrounding
brackets, so nesting can no longer hide one marker from the scan.

* perf(validate): cap the near-duplicate bullet scan at 400 bullets

duplicates::validate is an O(bullets²) pairwise Jaccard scan that ran
unbounded — a malformed or hostile "generated" document with thousands of
bullet-shaped lines held a tokio worker for seconds on every save.

Truncate to MAX_DUP_BULLETS (400) before the pairwise pass, mirroring the
count-cap discipline agent::tools_quality already uses. A pathological
bullet count now returns in well under 500ms and still flags a genuine
duplicate placed inside the cap.

* fix(validate): cap the content-report issue list to avoid silent report loss

An uncapped ContentReport.issues could grow the serialized report toward
~1MB on a pathological document (thousands of forged roles / duplicate
bullets). The IPC save path clamps quality_report to 256KB, truncating
that blob mid-JSON; merge_quality_report then fails to parse it and
silently falls back to the OLD stored report — a fresh report just
vanishes.

Cap the issue list at MAX_CONTENT_ISSUES (200) in validate_content itself,
so the byte clamp downstream is never reached. Criticals sort first before
truncation so a warning flood can never push a real Critical out of the
visible list; a trailing REPORT_TRUNCATED marker names the dropped count
instead of a silent cut.

* fix(validate): strip control chars from target-language input

normalize_language only trimmed leading/trailing whitespace before taking
the first 2 characters, so an internal control character (e.g. "a\nb")
survived into the 2-char result. That value reaches this module's own
validate:content span text and content.language_mismatch's evidence — a
log-injection primitive.

Filter to alphanumeric characters before taking the first 2. Also mirror
the Zod targetLanguage.max(32) cap server-side in resume_validate_content,
the same trust-boundary treatment every other field on that command
already gets.

* docs(agent): correct stale four-result-tags comment in the fence-tag registry

The comment claimed four super::tools_quality result tags were registered;
only three are. The fourth tool (lookup_salary) carries no free text to
fence and returns via envelope_result instead. Fix the comment so a future
fenced salary result isn't wrongly assumed already covered.

* fix(ai-generations): clamp quality_report on the bundle import path

The IPC save path already clamps quality_report to QUALITY_REPORT_MAX_BYTES
before persisting, but AiGenerationStore::import (a restored backup bundle
- an equally untrusted, user-supplied file) wrote the bundle's quality_report
straight to the column with no cap at all.

Move QUALITY_REPORT_MAX_BYTES into the data layer as the single source of
truth for both write paths, and clamp it in import too.

* docs: point at the content-issue code roster instead of copying its count

* fix(ai-generate): clear stale report before regenerating

handleGenerate cleared resumeOut/coverOut/buffers but never the quality
report, so the 'both'-mode progressive-reveal window (stage done while
the cover still streams) rendered the previous generation's report
against the new resume until persist recomputed one.

* fix(ai-generate): guard recheck against a mid-flight session reset

handleRecheck awaited validateContent.mutateAsync then unconditionally
called onReportChange with a stale closure's report/currentOutput — a
Reset during the in-flight call could re-inject a report into an
already-cleared session. Add an epoch ref bumped whenever meta/
sourceResume/jobAd change, checked before onReportChange fires.

* fix(quality-report): map the truncated-report code and add a message fallback

The synthetic report.truncated code had no i18n key, so it rendered the
generic quality.fallback sentence plus a bare count as evidence. Add
quality.issue.report.truncated (en + de) and make messageFor() fall
back to the Rust-authored issue.message before quality.fallback, so
any future unmapped code degrades to something meaningful.

* fix(validate): key accented project links without a utf-8 boundary panic

canonical_link stripped the scheme with `&s[..8]`, a fixed BYTE offset, so
any project URL whose 7th/8th byte fell inside a multibyte char aborted the
process: `www.café-berlin.de`, `http://éxample.com` and `ab.com/éx` all
panicked with "byte index 8 is not a char boundary". The release profile is
panic = "abort", so the app died mid-generation, before the document was
saved — a German or French project domain was enough to trigger it.

Byte-compare the scheme prefix on `as_bytes()` and only slice once the
prefix is known to be that (pure-ASCII) scheme. Audited the rest of
canonical_link and urls_in: every other boundary already comes from a
char-aware API (`trim`, `trim_end_matches`, `split_once`, regex match
spans), so this was the only fixed-offset cut.

Covered by a canonical_link unit test with a straddling char at each
boundary the function cuts at (2-, 3- and 4-byte widths), the three
reproducer URLs run through the full validate_content path, and an accented
link in the en source/paraphrase fixture pair so the fixture suite carries
it permanently.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(agent): order criticals first before compacting the issue list

compact_content_report took the first MAX_ISSUES issues in EMISSION order,
but validate_content emits in check order, not severity order. A draft that
tripped 20+ Warnings before a late check therefore dropped the Critical
itself — ats.header_in_body is emitted near the end — while the summary
still reported `criticals: 1`. The model saw a count it had no issue to act
on.

Stable-sort Criticals ahead of everything else before the cap; within each
severity the emission order is preserved, and the counts still reflect the
full report rather than the surfaced slice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: regenerate the workflow catalog

The catalog generator's output drifted from the committed README on
origin/main (heading style + this branch's new prompts-codegen CI step);
the pre-push gate diffs the regenerated output, so the regen must land
with the branch that trips it.

* fix: guard superseded generation catch from stomping a newer run's ui

The catch block in handleGenerate lacked the ownership guard its finally
block already had: a Regenerate click during an in-flight cover-letter
stream aborts run 1 after run 2 owns the UI, and run 1's late rejection
then reset stage/buffers/stage rotation out from under run 2. Early-return
when the controller ref no longer matches. Regression test covers the
supersede-during-stream window the stale-persist tests missed.

PR #963 review finding (MEDIUM, renderer race).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: clamp content issue message and evidence spans to byte caps

MAX_CONTENT_ISSUES bounds issue count but not size: ats.long_bullet
quotes the whole bullet verbatim (it fires because the bullet is long),
so a 200KB document could push a sub-report past the 256KB quality_report
budget and into the truncate-mid-JSON path M-3 exists to make
unreachable. Clamp message/evidence at the issue() chokepoint (400 bytes
each, char-boundary safe via clamp_to_bytes, truncation marker inside
the budget) so count x size is genuinely bounded.

PR #963 review finding (MEDIUM, correctness).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep merged quality report within the 256kb column budget

Both write paths clamp the incoming quality_report alone, so merging
onto a stored sub-report near the cap could persist up to twice the
documented budget. Guard at the sink: if the merged union exceeds
QUALITY_REPORT_MAX_BYTES, keep incoming whole (known-parseable and
within budget) instead of byte-truncating merged JSON, which would be
unparseable on the next read and silently revert to the stale report.

PR #963 review finding (LOW/MEDIUM, data).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: flag lone surrogates in the gen-prompts rust escape guard

Well-formed JSON.stringify (ES2019+) escapes an unpaired surrogate as
\uXXXX just like a control character, producing the same Rust-invalid
escape the guard exists to catch; valid astral pairs pass through raw
and stay fine. Rename hasControlChar to hasRustUnsafeChar to match.
Also corrects the stale pick_report reference in quality-report.ts:
the Rust merge is merge_quality_report and does not special-case '{}'.

PR #963 review findings (2x LOW, robustness + docs).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: anchor staleness hash per document slot and persist re-checks

sourceTextHash was a top-level sibling map, but quality_report merges
per top-level key: a resume-only regenerate emitted {resume} and the
merge wholesale-replaced the map, permanently orphaning the surviving
cover letter's staleness anchor (a later hand-edit then showed green on
text the report never saw). The wrapper is now schemaVersion 2 with the
hash inside each document slot ({report, sourceTextHash}), so the
generic per-key merge carries report and anchor atomically; v1 blobs
parse as no-report by design (unreleased shape, dev machines only).

Also unifies Re-check via a shared use-quality-recheck hook: TailorFlow
(the surface with inline editing) gains the previously missing Re-check
action, and both surfaces now persist the merged wrapper through the
save path's empty-keeps-existing merge rules instead of discarding the
result on reopen. Session-only fallback (commented + tested) when the
record has no job url to merge onto.

PR #963 round-2 review findings (MEDIUM staleness, LOW docs shape,
LOW/MEDIUM re-check split). Mutation-checked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: key re-check staleness guard off run starts, not input identity

The epoch guard in use-quality-recheck bumped only when meta/source/
job-ad identity changed, which covers Reset but not Regenerate (both
run paths reuse those references), so a slow re-check resolving after
a Regenerate click could resurrect a stale report and persist
pre-regenerate text over the fresh document. The epoch now also bumps
on every generating-flag transition; merge/persist read the live base
report and live texts at resolution time and drop the result if the

head_commit.message:
feat: deterministic content validation and quality report for generated documents (#963)

* feat: add evidence extraction module and move the bullet scorer out of match_resume

rank_trim_candidates' core moves verbatim into documents::evidence::rank_bullets,
which extract_evidence now reuses to structure the source resume into roles,
projects, education and an honest present/absent skill split for one posting.

match_resume keeps a TrimCandidate: From<EvidenceBullet> shim so the
match:trimSuggestions payload is wire-identical (three camelCase fields, score
still a JSON integer) and shrinks 1276 -> 1132 LOC.

keywords_normalized becomes a collect() over the new keywords_normalized_list so
occurrence-counting consumers share one tokenizer instead of forking it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: add deterministic content validators for generated resumes and letters

validate::content checks the text a model wrote against the candidate's own
resume, the posting, and the target language, before anything is rendered. The
rule it mechanically enforces: a model may never produce a Critical - every one
comes from a deterministic comparison against the source document.

24 issue codes in one table (6 Critical, 18 Warning); the constructor reads the
severity from that table so a code and its severity cannot drift. Pure L1 - no
Tauri, no AppHandle, no IO - and one languages_align decision drives every
resume-posting comparison, so a quality report can never contradict the match
score shown for the same pair.

False positives are the risk this module is designed around: every threshold is
a named const with a boundary test, 1900-2099 is excluded from metric checks,
the contact band is skipped, an open-ended source span resolved to a concrete
year is not a fabricated date, and an unusable posting or a wrong-language
output silences the derived comparisons instead of cascading. Three fixtures
assert a clean en resume, a clean de resume and a grounded letter produce
literally zero findings.

lexicon.rs is a hand-stub transcribing the anti-AI-tell lists from
packages/prompts natural-voice.ts; codegen replaces it behind the same
interface. Not implemented: the letter company-name check - ContentInput has no
company field and the frozen code vocabulary has no code for it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: point languages_align at its three real consumers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(prompts): export ai-tell word lists and template openers

Adds AI_TELL_LEXICAL_WORDS_*, AI_TELL_PROSE_WORDS_*, and TEMPLATE_OPENERS_*
arrays to natural-voice.ts as the discrete, codegen-consumable source of
truth behind the prose anti-AI-tell rulesets. The cover-letter prompt's
opener-ban examples now derive from TEMPLATE_OPENERS_EN/DE instead of
separately hand-authored strings, so the prompt bans exactly what the
Rust content validator (generated from these same arrays) checks for.

* feat(validate): generate the content-validator lexicon from prompts

Adds packages/prompts/scripts/gen-prompts-rust.ts (pnpm gen:prompts /
gen:prompts:check, mirroring gen-ipc-rust.ts) and replaces the hand-stubbed
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/validate/content/lexicon.rs with its generated
output, sourced directly from natural-voice.ts's word-list arrays so the
Rust validator can never drift from the prompt's own bans. Moves the
stub's unit tests into content/test.rs (generated files carry no
hand-authored tests) and wires gen:prompts:check into the same CI job
as gen:ipc:check.

* feat(agent): add four résumé-quality read tools to the agent registry

Add validate_resume, search_candidate_evidence, lookup_salary, and
get_trim_suggestions as thin adapters over validate::content,
documents::evidence, and salary_research (zero new business logic).
Split into a sibling agent/tools_quality.rs to stay under the R8
module-size cap, wired into read_tools()/prep_application_tools() via
one call. ToolContext now also carries resume_id so the SOURCE résumé
resolves server-side, never from model-supplied args. Raise
MAX_AGENT_STEPS 12 -> 14 for the two extra optional quality-tool turns
a run may now spend.

* feat(ai-generations): persist quality_report on the application aggregate

Add the deterministic content-quality report as a new column on the
ai_generations aggregate (ADR-007 addendum): additive migration,
AiGenerationRecord field, insert/update/import/row_to_record wiring, and
a pick-non-empty merge rule that also treats the migration's '{}'
placeholder as "no report" so it never clobbers a real one.

* feat(resume): add content-validation ipc command

Expose validate::content::validate_content over ipc as
resume_validate_content: a new zod schema + generated rust request
struct, a server-side-clamped tauri command, and the tauri-client
namespace wiring. Pure/deterministic, no ai call, safe to run on every save.

* feat(ai-generate): add quality-report validation lib and service hook

Renderer-side glue around resume:validateContent: computeQualityReport
(best-effort, never blocks/fails a save), the useValidateContent mutation
hook, and a canned clean-report mock-client stub for tests.

* feat(ai-generate): carry a fresh quality report on every generation save

Both surfaces (AI Generate's useGeneration, TailorFlow's generation-store)
now validate resumeText/coverLetterText right before persisting and attach
the report to the save request; the parsed report lands in session state
(additive report field) and cold-entry hydration seeds it back from a
saved record's qualityReport. Validation failure degrades to a report-less
save, never blocking or failing the generation itself.

* fix(ai-generations): merge quality_report per top-level wrapper key

pick_report treated the whole column as one opaque blob, so a letter-only
save (which only ever carries a coverLetter sub-report) clobbered a stored
resume sub-report and vice versa. Parse both sides as JSON objects and
overlay incoming's top-level keys onto existing's instead, so independent
resume/coverLetter saves layer the same way every other field on this
aggregate already does.

The add_quality_report migration is still unreleased on this branch, so
its default simplifies from '{}' to '' in place (no shipped build has
seen it) and the merge no longer needs a placeholder special case. Also
clamp the save-path quality_report to 256 KB, the same trust-boundary
treatment every other free-text field on this command gets.

* fix(resume): reject an unrecognized doc kind and drop the duplicate span

resume_validate_content silently coerced any unrecognized docKind to
DocKind::Resume and logged the raw request string twice (the command-level
span plus validate_content's own). Reject "resume"/"coverLetter" strictly
with a Validation error, and drop the command-level span entirely — the
inner validate_content span already logs codes/counts (ADR-027).

Add the command-level test coverage this file was missing: oversized
multi-byte inputs and an oversized requirements list are clamped rather
than processed whole (mirrors match_resume's own test), coverLetter
docKind routes to the letter ruleset instead of the résumé-structure
checks, and an unknown docKind is rejected.

* feat(ai-generate): add quality badge, report panel, and hand-edit nudge ui

QualityBadge (self-describing chip, opens QualityReportPanel), the panel
(issues grouped by section, severity chip, guidance-framed message per
issue code with a generic fallback for unknown codes, quoted evidence,
metrics footer), and HandEditNudge (dismissible, once per generation via a
remount key) — wired into both results surfaces. en/de i18n for all new
copy, keyed per issue code (quality.issue.<code>).

* fix(agent): close two fence-boundary forgery gaps in the quality tools

HIGH-1: register the three new agent/tools_quality.rs result tags
(validate_resume_result, search_candidate_evidence_result,
get_trim_suggestions_result) in FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS so a forged tag
smuggled into a job_posting body (or a sibling quality-tool result)
gets neutralized, not just the tag matching its own wrapper.

HIGH-1b: neutralize a forged bare [tool_result:{name}] marker inside
untrusted tool-result bodies before wrapping the real one around it —
FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS only covers the <tag> syntax, not this separate
transcript-boundary format.

Adds regression tests for both, including the critic's probe B (a
job_posting body carrying a forged validate_resume_result block) and
the sibling-tag case.

* fix(validate): stop content validators accusing truthful resumes

Six reproduced false-positive Criticals, each on a document that stated
nothing but the truth:

- project links compare on a canonical key (scheme dropped, host lowered,
  trailing slash removed) and report the verbatim span; a bare host now needs
  a path or a known code host, so a stack line's Socket.IO/Bun.sh no longer
  read as links, and the stack line is excluded structurally as well
- a role survives on any company token of two characters or more, so a
  shortened employer (IBM Deutschland GmbH written as IBM) is not a dropped
  role; legal forms and geography can never be the sole survival evidence
- the language Critical is withheld when the source resume reads as the same
  wrong language, which is detector disagreement rather than a defect, and
  the metrics survive with it
- unsupported_date no longer fires on a later year just because the source
  spelled its open end as seit 2021 / since 2021 / 2021 -, and open-ended
  detection now understands those spellings
- present-tense markers match whole words, so presented, knowledge, currently
  and actually stop reading as date context
- the second-contact-block Critical needs a real address and a name on the
  section's first line, not a bare @ next to any short line

Also: k/m/bn and doubled/2x restatements count as sourced numbers, metric
checks no longer skip every separator-laden body bullet, education entries
with date spans reach the evidence set, German function words are filtered
out of the skills split (locally, never in the scoring kernel's STOPWORDS),
stems never reach a user-facing message, low_coverage needs a five-point
drop, and the report's serialized key set is pinned against its TS mirror.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(validate): stop title_drift matching employers on a shared year

`titled_entries` splits an entry at its FIRST separator, so the date span stays
inside the company string and its year tokens join the company identity set.
Two unrelated employers whose spans merely touched the same year ("… | 2018 -
2021" and "… | 2015 - 2018") matched each other, and the second entry's title
was reported as drift from the first's.

Found by extending the German fixtures with a third role, which also gives the
German paraphrase fixture a shortened-company-name case (IBM Deutschland GmbH
written as IBM) so it discriminates the dropped_role survival rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(validate): correct two comments that overstated the contact-line rule

`metrics_in` no longer skips every `is_contact_shaped` line, and
`has_real_contact_match` has one caller, not two — `ats::is_contact_cluster`
applies the same rule inline because it also has to reject a date range that
`PHONE_RE` reads as a phone number.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ai-generate): detect stale quality reports after hand-edits

Wire a QualityReport.sourceTextHash (djb2 of the exact validated text) so
QualityBadge/QualityReportPanel can tell when resumeOut/coverOut has diverged
from what was checked - a hand-edit, or reopening a saved generation edited
since it was saved. A stale doc switches to a distinct "checked before your
edits" state instead of keeping a green "no issues" badge on text the report
never saw. The same hash comparison covers both the live session and cold
hydration for free, since staleness is derived at render time rather than
stored.

Also wires the previously-dead useValidateContent hook to a "Re-check" action
on the quality panel (AI Generate surface only, where source/jobAd/meta are
already local) that re-validates the current text and clears staleness.

* fix(ai-generate): stop a cancelled/regenerated run from persisting a stale quality report

Reproduced race: computeQualityReport() sits between generation finishing and
onComplete/save. cancel() aborts the controller and resets the session
synchronously, but the in-flight validation call keeps running past that
point - without a guard it resurrects the (now-reset) session with a stale
report and fires onComplete (the caller's save), silently persisting +
flipping "Applied" for a run the user cancelled.

- generation-store.ts: check controller.signal.aborted before patching the
  report / calling onComplete; ownership-guard the finally block's
  controller-map cleanup so a stale run's teardown can't clobber a newer run
  that already replaced it.
- useGeneration.ts: abort any prior controller when a fresh run starts
  (Regenerate re-entrancy), guard persist()'s setReport/save behind the same
  aborted check, and ownership-guard the finally block's isGenerating/ref
  cleanup the same way.
- AIGeneratePage's reset() aborted only while stage==='generating', missing
  the post-generation validation/save window (stage is already 'done' there)
  - broadened to abort whenever a run is in flight.

* fix(prompts): resolve lexicon-prompt drift, opener duplicates, codegen escaping

Removes 'not only'/'nicht nur'/'sondern auch' from the AI-tell prose arrays
(the prompt never bans them, or only asks to use them sparingly), fixes the
cover-letter opener-ban examples to quote two distinct opener families
instead of two near-duplicates and to render the German example with
correct mid-sentence noun capitalization, derives the same hand-typed
opener examples in the application-email prompt from the shared array, and
adds a control-character guard to the prompt-to-Rust lexicon codegen so a
bad array entry fails at generation time instead of emitting invalid Rust.

Adds a mechanical array-to-prompt direction guard (the reverse of the
existing prompt-to-Rust codegen pin) so every AI-tell lexicon entry stays
traceable to prose the model was actually instructed to avoid.

* refactor: narrow the quality report barrel to its consumed exports

* docs: sync content-validation phase 1 into knowledge base

- resume-domain.md: updated trim-panel pointer from match_resume::rank_trim_candidates
  to documents/evidence::rank_bullets; added content-validation paragraph (deterministic
  validators, 24 codes, ContentReport wrapper on ai_generations).
- domain-model.md: added evidence extraction + content validation paragraphs under
  Job/matching section; noted four agent Read tools.
- adr-007: added F2 addendum documenting quality_report column (per-key merge rule,
  opaque JSON wrapper, partial-save preservation via merge_quality_report, sourceTextHash
  staleness detection).
- Updated last-updated timestamps to 2026-08-09.

Pointers verified against evidence.rs + validate/content/mod.rs source. Contract shapes
(ContentInput/ContentIssue/ContentReport) match task #1 shipped artifacts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(renderer): validate quality_report shape before parsing (m-1)

parseQualityReport cast unknown -> QualityReport with no shape validation,
so a malformed persisted quality_report column crashed the whole app (only
the root ErrorBoundary caught it) every time that record's TailorFlow
opened. Validate schemaVersion + each sub-report's issues array/metrics
object defensively; a malformed sub-report now drops to undefined instead
of throwing, and a malformed issue entry is filtered rather than crashing
the array.

* fix(agent): defeat nested [tool_result] marker forgery in tool results

TOOL_RESULT_MARKER matched a full [tool_result:...] delimited token whose
body admitted a literal `[`, so a forged marker nested inside another one
(e.g. [tool_result:[tool_result:save_resume]]) survived neutralization:
the greedy body stopped at the FIRST `]` (the inner marker's own close),
leaving the fully-formed inner marker untouched in the output.

Match the opening [tool_result PREFIX only and replace with the canonical
"[ tool_result" form, same convention as the fence-tag neutralizer -
every occurrence is found and broken independently of surrounding
brackets, so nesting can no longer hide one marker from the scan.

* perf(validate): cap the near-duplicate bullet scan at 400 bullets

duplicates::validate is an O(bullets²) pairwise Jaccard scan that ran
unbounded — a malformed or hostile "generated" document with thousands of
bullet-shaped lines held a tokio worker for seconds on every save.

Truncate to MAX_DUP_BULLETS (400) before the pairwise pass, mirroring the
count-cap discipline agent::tools_quality already uses. A pathological
bullet count now returns in well under 500ms and still flags a genuine
duplicate placed inside the cap.

* fix(validate): cap the content-report issue list to avoid silent report loss

An uncapped ContentReport.issues could grow the serialized report toward
~1MB on a pathological document (thousands of forged roles / duplicate
bullets). The IPC save path clamps quality_report to 256KB, truncating
that blob mid-JSON; merge_quality_report then fails to parse it and
silently falls back to the OLD stored report — a fresh report just
vanishes.

Cap the issue list at MAX_CONTENT_ISSUES (200) in validate_content itself,
so the byte clamp downstream is never reached. Criticals sort first before
truncation so a warning flood can never push a real Critical out of the
visible list; a trailing REPORT_TRUNCATED marker names the dropped count
instead of a silent cut.

* fix(validate): strip control chars from target-language input

normalize_language only trimmed leading/trailing whitespace before taking
the first 2 characters, so an internal control character (e.g. "a\nb")
survived into the 2-char result. That value reaches this module's own
validate:content span text and content.language_mismatch's evidence — a
log-injection primitive.

Filter to alphanumeric characters before taking the first 2. Also mirror
the Zod targetLanguage.max(32) cap server-side in resume_validate_content,
the same trust-boundary treatment every other field on that command
already gets.

* docs(agent): correct stale four-result-tags comment in the fence-tag registry

The comment claimed four super::tools_quality result tags were registered;
only three are. The fourth tool (lookup_salary) carries no free text to
fence and returns via envelope_result instead. Fix the comment so a future
fenced salary result isn't wrongly assumed already covered.

* fix(ai-generations): clamp quality_report on the bundle import path

The IPC save path already clamps quality_report to QUALITY_REPORT_MAX_BYTES
before persisting, but AiGenerationStore::import (a restored backup bundle
- an equally untrusted, user-supplied file) wrote the bundle's quality_report
straight to the column with no cap at all.

Move QUALITY_REPORT_MAX_BYTES into the data layer as the single source of
truth for both write paths, and clamp it in import too.

* docs: point at the content-issue code roster instead of copying its count

* fix(ai-generate): clear stale report before regenerating

handleGenerate cleared resumeOut/coverOut/buffers but never the quality
report, so the 'both'-mode progressive-reveal window (stage done while
the cover still streams) rendered the previous generation's report
against the new resume until persist recomputed one.

* fix(ai-generate): guard recheck against a mid-flight session reset

handleRecheck awaited validateContent.mutateAsync then unconditionally
called onReportChange with a stale closure's report/currentOutput — a
Reset during the in-flight call could re-inject a report into an
already-cleared session. Add an epoch ref bumped whenever meta/
sourceResume/jobAd change, checked before onReportChange fires.

* fix(quality-report): map the truncated-report code and add a message fallback

The synthetic report.truncated code had no i18n key, so it rendered the
generic quality.fallback sentence plus a bare count as evidence. Add
quality.issue.report.truncated (en + de) and make messageFor() fall
back to the Rust-authored issue.message before quality.fallback, so
any future unmapped code degrades to something meaningful.

* fix(validate): key accented project links without a utf-8 boundary panic

canonical_link stripped the scheme with `&s[..8]`, a fixed BYTE offset, so
any project URL whose 7th/8th byte fell inside a multibyte char aborted the
process: `www.café-berlin.de`, `http://éxample.com` and `ab.com/éx` all
panicked with "byte index 8 is not a char boundary". The release profile is
panic = "abort", so the app died mid-generation, before the document was
saved — a German or French project domain was enough to trigger it.

Byte-compare the scheme prefix on `as_bytes()` and only slice once the
prefix is known to be that (pure-ASCII) scheme. Audited the rest of
canonical_link and urls_in: every other boundary already comes from a
char-aware API (`trim`, `trim_end_matches`, `split_once`, regex match
spans), so this was the only fixed-offset cut.

Covered by a canonical_link unit test with a straddling char at each
boundary the function cuts at (2-, 3- and 4-byte widths), the three
reproducer URLs run through the full validate_content path, and an accented
link in the en source/paraphrase fixture pair so the fixture suite carries
it permanently.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(agent): order criticals first before compacting the issue list

compact_content_report took the first MAX_ISSUES issues in EMISSION order,
but validate_content emits in check order, not severity order. A draft that
tripped 20+ Warnings before a late check therefore dropped the Critical
itself — ats.header_in_body is emitted near the end — while the summary
still reported `criticals: 1`. The model saw a count it had no issue to act
on.

Stable-sort Criticals ahead of everything else before the cap; within each
severity the emission order is preserved, and the counts still reflect the
full report rather than the surfaced slice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: regenerate the workflow catalog

The catalog generator's output drifted from the committed README on
origin/main (heading style + this branch's new prompts-codegen CI step);
the pre-push gate diffs the regenerated output, so the regen must land
with the branch that trips it.

* fix: guard superseded generation catch from stomping a newer run's ui

The catch block in handleGenerate lacked the ownership guard its finally
block already had: a Regenerate click during an in-flight cover-letter
stream aborts run 1 after run 2 owns the UI, and run 1's late rejection
then reset stage/buffers/stage rotation out from under run 2. Early-return
when the controller ref no longer matches. Regression test covers the
supersede-during-stream window the stale-persist tests missed.

PR #963 review finding (MEDIUM, renderer race).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: clamp content issue message and evidence spans to byte caps

MAX_CONTENT_ISSUES bounds issue count but not size: ats.long_bullet
quotes the whole bullet verbatim (it fires because the bullet is long),
so a 200KB document could push a sub-report past the 256KB quality_report
budget and into the truncate-mid-JSON path M-3 exists to make
unreachable. Clamp message/evidence at the issue() chokepoint (400 bytes
each, char-boundary safe via clamp_to_bytes, truncation marker inside
the budget) so count x size is genuinely bounded.

PR #963 review finding (MEDIUM, correctness).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep merged quality report within the 256kb column budget

Both write paths clamp the incoming quality_report alone, so merging
onto a stored sub-report near the cap could persist up to twice the
documented budget. Guard at the sink: if the merged union exceeds
QUALITY_REPORT_MAX_BYTES, keep incoming whole (known-parseable and
within budget) instead of byte-truncating merged JSON, which would be
unparseable on the next read and silently revert to the stale report.

PR #963 review finding (LOW/MEDIUM, data).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: flag lone surrogates in the gen-prompts rust escape guard

Well-formed JSON.stringify (ES2019+) escapes an unpaired surrogate as
\uXXXX just like a control character, producing the same Rust-invalid
escape the guard exists to catch; valid astral pairs pass through raw
and stay fine. Rename hasControlChar to hasRustUnsafeChar to match.
Also corrects the stale pick_report reference in quality-report.ts:
the Rust merge is merge_quality_report and does not special-case '{}'.

PR #963 review findings (2x LOW, robustness + docs).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: anchor staleness hash per document slot and persist re-checks

sourceTextHash was a top-level sibling map, but quality_report merges
per top-level key: a resume-only regenerate emitted {resume} and the
merge wholesale-replaced the map, permanently orphaning the surviving
cover letter's staleness anchor (a later hand-edit then showed green on
text the report never saw). The wrapper is now schemaVersion 2 with the
hash inside each document slot ({report, sourceTextHash}), so the
generic per-key merge carries report and anchor atomically; v1 blobs

* fix: size the quality-report byte cap for json escaping, not raw bytes

QUALITY_REPORT_MAX_BYTES was sized from the RAW per-field caps in
validate/content (~214 KB per sub-report), but serde_json escaping roughly
doubles quote/backslash-heavy text: a legitimate two-sub-report wrapper full
of quoted resume evidence serializes to ~780 KB — past the old 512 KiB cap —
and sanitize_quality_report would silently drop it to the empty sentinel.
Resize to 1 MiB (2x, matching the documented <=2x escape-density assumption
for realistic text) with the escaped arithmetic in the doc comment, add a
regression test that measures the actual serialized bytes of a quote-filled
worst case (asserts it exceeds the old cap AND survives the new one), and
refresh the two validate/content doc comments that cited the old 512 KiB
figure. The round-6 worst-case test filled fields with 'x' — non-escaping
filler never stressed the expansion the cap exists to absorb.

head_commit.message:
fix: link orphaned landing routes from home and add sitemap lastmod (#962)

Search Console reported /agent-system, /architecture-map, /how-it-works and
/accessibility as "Discovered - currently not indexed" with last-crawled N/A,
and has not queued /tech-radar at all. Nothing was blocking them: all return
200, none carry noindex, robots.txt is Allow: /, and the sitemap reads Success.

The home page footer had drifted from the doc-page SiteFooter — /agent-system,
/architecture-map, /tech-radar and /storybook/ were reachable only from pages
Google has not fetched yet, so they sat one hop behind an uncrawled page. / is
the only URL with real crawl equity. This is the same orphan class #934 fixed
for /how-it-works, so HomeBody.test.tsx now asserts every sitemap route is
linked from home; it fails today if any link is removed.

Sitemap entries also carry a hand-kept lastmod from each route's last
content-bearing commit, rather than a build-time timestamp that would churn on
every deploy.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
